question: What is the primary purpose of a digital folder on a computer?

options.A: To group and store related files together
options.B: To increase the processing speed of the computer
options.C: To convert text files into spreadsheet formats

explanation: Folders act like physical file drawers in an office, helping you keep similar documents together so they are easy to find later. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is proper digital file management important for a healthcare worker?

options.A: It stops computer hardware from ever experiencing mechanical failure
options.B: It ensures patient records and clinic documents remain organized and accessible
options.C: It prevents unauthorized persons from turning on the computer
options.D: It automatically prints out physical copies of daily clinic attendance

explanation: Keeping a tidy digital workspace saves time during busy clinical hours and prevents important patient information from getting lost. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which action is typically required first when creating a new folder on a computer desktop?

options.D: Pressing the power button for five seconds

explanation: Right-clicking an open area on the desktop or inside another window brings up a menu that includes the option to create a new folder. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is a major risk of leaving newly created folders with default names like 'New Folder'?

options.A: The operating system will block you from saving data inside them
options.B: The computer system will automatically delete them after 24 hours
options.C: It makes finding specific patient documents later much more difficult
options.D: Files inside them cannot be edited by spreadsheet applications

explanation: Default names provide no information about the contents, leading to confusion and wasted search time during clinical shifts. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What does the 'Save As' command allow you to do that a basic 'Save' does not?

options.A: Instantly print the document to the nearest network printer
options.B: Choose a new name and destination folder for the document
options.C: Send the document directly to the national health database
options.D: Automatically check the text for spelling and grammar errors

explanation: Save As prompts you to specify where the file goes and what it is called, which is useful when creating a duplicate or saving a brand new file. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is frequent saving particularly crucial for computer users in areas with unstable power supply?

options.A: To prevent the permanent loss of unsaved work during sudden electricity cuts
options.B: To allow multiple midwives to type in the same document at once
options.C: To speed up the internet connection for downloading patient forms
options.D: To make the computer screen brighter and easier to read during the day

explanation: Unsaved data lives only in the computer's temporary memory and vanishes instantly if the power fails without a backup battery. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main difference between copying a file and moving a file?

options.A: Copying changes the file format, whereas moving keeps the format the same
options.B: Copying permanently deletes the file, whereas moving saves it to a flash drive
options.C: Copying leaves the original file in place while creating a duplicate, whereas moving relocates it entirely
options.D: Copying requires an internet connection, whereas moving works offline

explanation: Copying results in two identical files in different spots, while moving simply changes the address or folder where the single file lives. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h4)

question: A midwife wants to send a monthly maternity report to the hospital director while keeping her own master copy safe in her department folder. What should she do?

options.A: Delete the report file so nobody else can read the statistics
options.B: Move the master report file directly into the director's folder
options.C: Rename the report file extension to a different format
options.D: Copy the report file and place the duplicate in the director's folder

explanation: Copying allows her to share a duplicate version of the document while keeping her original master file secure in its original location. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a subfolder in the context of computer file organization?

options.A: A backup copy of a document stored on an external flash drive
options.B: A temporary file that automatically deletes itself after shutdown
options.C: A folder placed inside another parent folder to create a hierarchy
options.D: An application used to open compressed archive documents

explanation: Subfolders live inside larger parent folders, allowing you to break down broad categories into smaller, specific groupings. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is a hierarchical folder structure better than keeping all files in one large folder?

options.A: It doubles the physical storage capacity of the computer hard drive
options.B: It automatically encrypts all medical data against cyber threats
options.C: It speeds up file retrieval and reduces clutter by grouping related items logically
options.D: It prevents the computer from ever needing software updates

explanation: Breaking documents down into categorized folders and subfolders makes navigation intuitive and prevents administrative chaos. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which practice helps ensure files are easily sorted in chronological order within a folder?

options.A: Writing file names in lowercase letters only
options.B: Using only random numbers as file titles
options.C: Including dates clearly in the file names
options.D: Keeping all documents saved on the desktop screen

explanation: Starting file names with dates (such as year and month) causes the operating system to arrange them neatly in order of creation time. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of regularly backing up critical clinic files to an external drive or cloud storage?

options.A: It allows the computer screen to display higher-resolution images
options.B: It removes the need to ever organize your computer folders
options.C: It stops office computers from gathering dust on their keyboards
options.D: It protects vital records from being lost permanently if the main computer breaks

explanation: Hardware failure or theft can destroy a primary machine, making external backups essential for preserving irreplaceable health data. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h6)
